guide.title: How to use AgroAI Advisor
guide.lead: This page explains what each part of the website does and how to use it, step by step.

banner.title: New here?
banner.body: Read a short guide to what AgroAI Advisor can do and how to use it.

s1.b: After you log in you land on your dashboard. It shows your recent crop checks, today's weather and the crops you grow.

s2.b: Under "About your farm", add the crops you grow and a short note. The advisor uses this to make its advice fit your farm.

s3.t: Check a crop or ask a question
s3.b: Tap "Check a crop" to send a photo, or "Ask a question" to type or speak.

s4.t: Follow the steps, or ask a person
s4.b: Read what to do. If it is serious, or I am not sure, send the summary to an extension officer.

check.b: Choose the crop, take a photo of the leaf or plant that worries you, and add a few words about what you noticed. You get what I see, why I think so, how sure I am, and what to do.

ask.b: Type your question, or hold the microphone button and speak. Ask about pests, planting, or whether you can spray today. You can fix the words before you send.

weather.b: Choose your town to see the weather now and for the next 5 days, with a plain note on what it means for your farm.

farm.b: On the dashboard, add your crops and notes. Saved checks and recent chats are remembered, so the advice is about your farm and not farms in general.

account.b: Change the text size, colour theme, and whether answers are read aloud. You can also delete your history or your whole account.

language.b: Use the English and Pidgin buttons at the top of the page to switch language at any time.

photo.title: Taking a good photo
tips: Come close, so the leaf fills the picture.
Hold the phone steady and use good daylight.
Photograph the part that worries you, not the whole field.
If the photo is blurry, take another. I will tell you if I need a clearer one.
Add a few words, such as "leaves are turning yellow". It helps.

read.title: How to read an answer
read.body: "How sure I am" tells you how much to trust it: Sure, Fairly sure or Not sure. "What could change my mind" lists things to check on your farm. Start with the low-cost steps under "What to do". It never gives a chemical dose: always follow the product label and your extension officer.

limits.title: What to keep in mind
limits.body: It can be wrong, and it cannot touch your plants or test your soil. If the plants are getting worse quickly, or many are affected, see an extension officer.

privacy.title: Your privacy
privacy.body: Your photos are never stored. Your account keeps your crop checks (the answer only) and your recent chat, and nobody else can see them. You can delete them at any time in My account.

landing.title: Clear, practical help for your farm, in English or Pidgin.
landing.lead: Take a photo of a sick leaf, ask a question by voice or by typing, and get advice that fits your weather and your crops. When I am not sure, I say so and point you to an extension officer.

s1.b: Photograph the leaf or plant that worries you. Add a few words about what you noticed.

s2.t: Get reasons, not just a verdict
s2.b: You see what I see, why I think so, how sure I am, and what would change my mind.

s3.b: Follow simple steps that start with low-cost methods. If it is serious or I am unsure, send the summary to an extension officer.

example.label: Example of an answer
example.see: Twisted leaves with pale yellow and green patches, and a smaller plant than its neighbours.
example.step: Pull out the worst plants today and burn or bury them, so whiteflies cannot carry the virus on.
example.note: An illustration of the layout, not a real farmer's result.

crops.title: Crops it knows well
crops.body: Cassava, yam, maize, plantain, cocoyam and pepper, with the pests and diseases common in Akwa Ibom. For other crops it gives general advice and tells you it knows less.

remember.title: Advice that knows your farm
remember.body: With an account, I remember your town, the crops you grow, and what happened before, so the advice is about your farm and not about farms in general. Your photos are never stored, and you can delete everything at any time.

honest.title: What it cannot do
honest.body: It can be wrong. It cannot touch your plants or test your soil. For animals, health, money or legal questions please see the right professional. It will never give a chemical dose: always follow the label and your extension officer.
